f.title: A stored paragraph written as CCaR writes column 23 ("1.2.1 - Organizational") is read two ways: flagged "not in the estimate" in some places, treated as 1.2.1 in others, and silently rewritten when you save any other field in the edit box
f.area: W2 pickers / stored paragraph kept, never rewritten
f.where: wbsUnlisted() and matBulk().wbs.get (and W1's aceWbsOf) read the stored text with aceNormWbs. wbsPathOf, wbsFieldSay, wbsPickedIn, srcWbsParts and wbsTake read it with wbsCodeIn (the text before a spaced dash). wbsPickedIn() is called from erUpdate() when the box opens (also from uipSay and from arUpdate on a From-another-year finish), and it rewrites the field.
f.scenario:
Before v2.12, a requirement's WBS was typed as "1.2.1 - Organizational" (pasted from CCaR's Spares WBS column). 1.2.1 is a paragraph of the estimate.

What the person sees:
- Needs attention shows ≠ 1 WBS not in the estimate.
- The WBS panel flags the line "⚠ not a paragraph … kept as stored".
- The edit box shows it as a valid paragraph, named "1.2.1 — Manpower › Maintenance › Organizational".
- The Spend Plan Source sends "1.2.1 - Organizational".
- The ACE tie-out's split claims "1.2.1-ORGANIZATIONAL", which matches no line.

Steps: open the edit box (📋), type only a new description, Save.

What happens: S.wbs is rewritten to "1.2.1", and the status says "saved WBS, Description". With nothing typed at all, next ↓ asks "Discard what you typed for B event…?".

Should: a stored paragraph is read by one rule everywhere. It is never rewritten by opening the box or by saving another field. A box with nothing typed asks nothing.

1 Needs attention wbsx lists B: [["B",["1.2.1 - Organizational"]]]
2 WBS panel: "wbsnm off | ⚠ not a paragraph of the 2026ACE estimate for O&M — kept as stored"
3 Spend Plan Source col 23: ["1.2.1 - Organizational"]
4 aceWbsOf: ["1.2.1-ORGANIZATIONAL"]
5 edit box opened, nothing typed: field "1.2.1", note "1.2.1 — Manpower › Maintenance › Organizational", erDirty true
6 next ↓ asks: ["Discard what you typed for B event and open C event?"]
7 after Save of the description only: S.wbs.B = [{"w":"1.2.1","v":[]}], status "✎ B event: saved WBS, Description."

Also p1c-ask.mjs. Control: C, stored as "1.3", asks nothing and moves on.
f.fix:
1. Use one reader for a stored paragraph's code: wbsCodeIn, the reading srcWbsPara and wbsTake already use. Apply it in wbsUnlisted, in matBulk().wbs.get, and in aceWbsOf (W1).
2. In erUpdate, uipSay and arUpdate, skip wbsPickedIn while the field still holds the stored text: compare against V.wbs, `was`, or arFin.wbsFrom.

- One stored value is flagged "not in the estimate" by wbsUnlisted (Needs attention, the WBS panel), matBulk().wbs.get and aceWbsOf.

f.title: Coverage counts requirements as having a WBS while their lines go out blank, and the export sends people to a Needs attention list that does not show them
f.area: W2 Needs attention / the WBS on a requirement vs the Spend Plan Source
f.where:
wbsStateOf() and attLists() decide `has` and the coverage from the stored lines only. srcWbsParts() / srcRowsOf() emit a blank-WBS line for:
- a split's unassigned remainder;
- a prime's lane money its CLIN grid carries nothing for (clinSplit returns []).
srcNoWbsSay() always ends "(Needs attention lists them)".
f.scenario:
Case (a): a prime whose only CLIN carries USAF and is on 1.2.1. The prime also draws ANG $50.
- The Spend Plan Source sends a $50 ANG line with a blank WBS.
- The status says to pick one in the requirement's record, and that Needs attention lists them.
- Needs attention's Without a WBS is empty; its coverage reads 4 of 4 requirements, $330 of $330 funded.
- A prime's record has no requirement-level WBS field.

Case (b): a split leaving $30 unassigned. Its blank line is named the same way, and Needs attention does not list it.

Case (c), the reverse: a requirement switched from OGC to Prime keeps its old S.wbs, and has no CLINs yet.
- Needs attention lists it as without a WBS.
- The Spend Plan Source sends that old paragraph on every line ("1.2.2 - Depot").

Should: the coverage and the list say exactly what the export will send blank. The message names where each blank line is fixed.

- A's lines: [[100,"1.2.1 - Organizational","0001"],[50,"",""]]
- export says: "⚠ 1 line goes out with no WBS paragraph, on 1 requirement: A event — pick one in each requirement’s record (Needs attention lists them)."
- Needs attention Without a WBS: [], coverage {n:4, of:4, f:330, fof:330}

Probe p2-src.mjs:
- B (a split leaving 30 unassigned) is named by the export; Needs attention lists only ["D"].
- D (a prime with no CLINs, S.wbs 1.2.2) goes out as "1.2.2 - Depot"; wbsStateOf(D) = {prime:true, has:false}.

- srcRowsOf's lines:
  - A: [100,"1.2.1 - Organizational","0001"] and [50,"",""]
  - B: 30 "1.2.1", 20 "1.3" and 30 blank
  - D: [40,"1.2.2 - Depot"]
- srcNoWbsSay: "⚠ 2 lines go out with no WBS paragraph, on 2 requirements: A event, B event — pick one in each requirement’s record (Needs attention lists them)."
- attLists().wbs: only ["D"]. The heading as drawn reads "3 of 4 requirements have one · $290 of $330 funded". Going by the export, only $250 of the $330 goes out with a WBS.
- wbsStateOf: A {prime, has:true}, B has:true, D {prime, has:false}.

**Why it is the code**
- For a service the CLIN grid carries nothing for, clinSplit returns [], so emitW calls srcWbsParts with clin null. That reads the requirement-level S.wbs, which a prime normally does not have, so the line goes out blank.
- wbsStateOf only asks whether each CLIN that carries money has a paragraph. It never asks whether the CLINs cover every service the lanes pay.
- For a split, wbsLinesHas counts it as having a WBS, while wbsResolve puts the unassigned remainder on a blank line.

**Each case is reachable by a person**

- (b) wbsAdd starts the second line at 0, so a split that does not add up to the whole is ordinary too.
- (c) In the edit box, clicking Prime and then Save:

  - hides the field, and its note says "a prime contract’s WBS is logged per CLIN";

- The false part is the builder's own wording, which nothing in contract.md or notes-W2.md covers:
  - "(Needs attention lists them)": A and B are not on that list.
  - "pick one in each requirement’s record": a prime's record has no WBS field.
- The contract defines Without a WBS by "any CLIN with money has none", so A's absence from the list follows the stated rule. The coverage heading's "funded dollars with a WBS" counts A's and B's blank dollars, which is open to argument: decision 6 in notes-W2.md says how coverage is counted, but not how blank remainders count.

**Severity**
Overstated. No figure in the file is wrong, and blank lines are part of the design. The defect is a status line that sends people to a list and a field that do not show the problem, plus a list and an export that disagree in case (c). Moderate, not major.

  - a prime's money on a service its CLIN grid does not carry (case a; fixed in the CLIN drill, since a prime's record has no WBS field);
  - a split's unassigned remainder (case b; fixed in its WBS split).
- Needs attention's coverage ($290 of $330) counts dollars that go out blank ($80), and $250 is what actually goes out with a WBS. The contract's "a prime is without one when any CLIN with money has none" allows this reading, so this part is a matter of interpretation, not a breach.
- Case (c), reached through the edit box's Prime button and Save: a prime with no CLINs keeps its old S.wbs, hidden from every box. Needs attention lists it as without a WBS, while the Spend Plan Source sends that paragraph ("1.2.2 - Depot") and does not name it.

votes.corrected:
Moderate, not major (no dollar is wrong). There are three defects:

1. **The export points to a list that does not hold the requirement.** srcNoWbsSay always ends "pick one in each requirement's record (Needs attention lists them)". Both claims are false for two kinds of blank line:
   - a split's unassigned remainder (the requirement has paragraphs, so Without a WBS does not list it);
   - a prime's money on a service its CLIN grid carries nothing for. clinSplit returns [], the line falls back to S.wbs, which is empty for a prime. The record cannot set it, and only the CLIN drill can.

   srcNoWbsSay should name where each kind is fixed: the record, the WBS split, or the CLIN drill. It should mention Needs attention only for requirements that list actually shows.

2. **Without a WBS's coverage overstates.** It counts every funded dollar of a requirement with any paragraph as "with a WBS". On the case (a) board it reads $330 of $330 while $50 goes out blank. In case (b), B's $80 is counted though $30 goes out blank. Coverage should count the funded dollars of the lines that actually carry a paragraph.

3. **A prime's leftover requirement-level S.wbs is read two ways.** togglePtype and reqApply leave S.wbs in place when a requirement becomes a prime:
   - srcWbsParts sends it on the prime's non-CLIN lines;
   - wbsStateOf ignores it, so Needs attention lists the prime as without a WBS, and its why-text says the lines go out blank.

   Decide in one place whether that S.wbs counts.

Under the contract's rule, the Without a WBS list itself is correct for (a) and (b). Listing those requirements there is a design change Brad can choose; it is not a breach.

f.title: The WBS quick box (Classify's WBS cell) drops typing on Esc without asking; the in-app prompt asked before v2.12
f.area: W2 quick box / the box controller
f.where: #uipVal markup now carries oninput="uipSay()". The box controller (the input listener near line 37853) never marks a field with an oninput attribute as pending, so dlgDirty() is false. uiPrompt now always uses the in-app box when given a list.
f.scenario:
Steps:
1. Open Classify.
2. Click a requirement's WBS cell. The quick box opens.
3. Type 1.2.2.
4. Press Esc.

Shows: the box closes without a question, and the typing is lost.

Should: ask "Discard what you typed?", as the edit box does for the same typing. The in-app prompt did ask at the slot commit, on the path where it was used.
